Container.Name: media-audit
Container.Overview: Scans your media library (read-only) and reports what's actually in it: size per movie/show/season, and container, codecs, resolution, HDR10/HDR10+/Dolby Vision, Atmos/DTS:X, audio and subtitle languages and release group for every file. Browse it all in the web UI.[br][br]The container keeps running: it serves the web UI and rescans on a schedule (03:00 daily by default), and the Scans page has a Scan now button. Rescans only re-read new or changed files.[br][br]On the very first start it writes /config/config.yml from the folders it finds under /media and does not scan until you press Scan now, so you can review the library list first. The web UI has no login; keep it on your LAN.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Config file and SQLite database. Keep this on the cache/appdata share, not on the media array.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Folder containing your libraries (e.g. movies/, tv/). Mounted read-only; media-audit never modifies files.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the scanner runs as (99 = nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the scanner runs as (100 = users).

Config.Name: Scan schedule
Config.Description: Optional. When to rescan, as a cron expression in the TZ time zone (0 3 * * * = 03:00 daily, 0 */6 * * * = every 6 hours), or off. Empty uses scan.schedule from config.yml (03:00 daily by default).

Config.Name: Scan workers
Config.Description: Files analyzed in parallel. Keep low (1-4) for array disks.
